Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

  "output_head": "# Helpdesk API
Rails 8.1 API-only backend for the helpdesk SaaS. The frontend is a separate app.
All endpoints live under `/api/v1` and speak JSON.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0 (see `.ruby-version`) and PostgreSQL. `DATABASE_URL` configures the
primary connection, for example:

    export DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql"
    bundle install
    bin/rails db:prepare
    bin/rails server            # Puma, on $PORT (default 3000)

Tests run against a separate database derived from `DATABASE_URL` (`helpdesk_development`
becomes `helpdesk_test`), or against `TEST_DATABASE_URL` if it is set:

    bin/rails test

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none | PostgreSQL connection |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Base URL for verification and reset links. Also the only browser origin allowed by CORS. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for outgoing email |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, none, none | SMTP delivery (production). Development writes mail to `tmp/mails/`. |
| `SECRET_KEY_BASE` | none | Required by Rails in production, even though the API does not use cookies. |

## Conventions

- **Business header:** every endpoint except `POST /api/v1/account/create` needs
  `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`. The header selects the business, and a session token only works within the business that issued it.
- **Sessions:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Errors:** `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...}}}`. Common codes:
  `account_required` (400), `parameter_missing` (400), `invalid_json` (400), `unauthorized` (401),
  `invalid_credentials` (401), `email_not_verified` (403), `user_suspended` (403), `account_cancelled` (403),
  `forbidden` (403), `account_not_found` (404), `validation_failed` (422), `invalid_token` (422),
  `invalid_current_password` (422), `already_cancelled` / `not_cancelled` / `reactivation_expired` (422),
  `already_accepted` / `already_revoked` (422).
  A field sent in the wrong shape, such as `"comment": "text"` where an object belongs, is also `validation_failed` (422).
- **Timestamps** are ISO 8601 UTC. Record IDs are integers.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /account/create` | none | Register a business and its owner (admin). Sends a verification email. | 201 `{account, user, message}` |
| `GET /portal` | header | Public business name and subdomain. | 200 `{portal: {name, subdomain}}` |
| `POST /sessions` | header | Sign in. The email must be verified. | 201 `{session: {id, token}, user, account}` |
| `DELETE /session` | token | Sign out this session. | 204 |
| `GET /account` | token | Full account, including cancellation status. | 200 `{account}` |
| `POST /account/cancel` | owner | Cancel the business and revoke all its sessions. | 200 `{account}` |
| `POST /account/reactivate` | owner | Reactivate within 90 days of cancellation. | 200 `{account}` |
| `GET /me` | token | Current user. | 200 `{user}` |
| `PATCH /me` | token | Update the name: `{"user":{"name":"Jo Smith"}}`. | 200 `{user}` |
| `PUT /me/password` | token | `{"password_change":{"current_password":"...","password":"..."}}`. Signs out all sessions. | 200 `{message}` |
| `POST /email_verifications` | header | `{"email_verification":{"email":"..."}}`. Emails a new link, replacing the old one. | 202 |
| `POST /email_verifications/confirm` | header | `{"email_verification":{"token":"..."}}`. | 200 `{user}` |
| `POST /password_resets` | header | `{"password_reset":{"email":"..."}}`. Emails a new reset link, replacing the old one. | 202 |
| `POST /password_resets/confirm` | header | `{"password_reset":{"token":"...","password":"..."}}`. Signs out all sessions. | 200 `{message}` |
| `POST /registrations` | header | Customer sign-up for the portal: `{"user":{"name":"...","email":"...","password":"..."}}`. Sends a verification email. The role is always `customer`. | 201 `{user, message}` |
| `GET /requests` | token | The signed-in user's own requests, most recently active first. Filter with `?status=open\|pending\|solved`. Paginated. | 200 `{requests, count, page, per_page, next_page, previous_page}` |
| `POST /requests` | token | Open a request: `{"request":{"subject":"...","comment":{"body":"..."}}}`. It starts `open`. | 201 `{request}` |
| `GET /requests/:id` | token | One of your requests. Other people's requests return 404. | 200 `{request}` |
| `PATCH /requests/:id` | token | Reply: `{"request":{"comment":{"body":"..."}}}`. Optionally add `"status":"solved"`. | 200 `{request}` |
| `GET /requests/:id/comments` | token | Public comments on your request, oldest first. Paginated. | 200 `{comments, count, page, per_page, next_page, previous_page}` |
| `GET /tickets` | staff | Every request in the business, most recently active first, with request",
  "output_tail": "id=<id>` for one person's tickets, or `assignee_id=unassigned` for tickets nobody is working.
  - `requester_id=<id>` for one customer's requests.
  - `q=<text>` finds a case-insensitive match in subjects and public comments. Private notes are never searched.
    `q` is literal text: `%`, `_`, and `\` match themselves, not wildcards. A blank `q` is ignored.
  - A value outside the allowed values, or an ID that is not a positive whole number, returns `422 validation_failed`.
  - Each ticket appears once, however many of its comments match, and `count` reflects the filtered total.
- **Customer filtering.** Customers can filter their own requests with `?status=`, and nothing else. The staff-only filters
  (`priority`, `assignee_id`, `requester_id`, and `q`) are ignored on `/requests`, so they reveal nothing about other requests.
- **Internal activity does not change the customer's request.** A private note, a priority change, an assignment, or an assignment cleared
  by suspension leaves `updated_at` and the request's place in the customer's list as they were. Only a public reply or
  a status change counts as activity.
- A private note is added through the same input: `{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking with billing.","public":false}}}`.

### Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, maximum 100). Each list returns `count`
(the total across all pages), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page`, and `previous_page`. The last two are `null`
when there is no such page. A value that is not a positive whole number returns `422 validation_failed`.

## Invitations and people

Admins invite people to the business as `admin` or `agent`. Customers join through registration instead.

- The emailed link is `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`. Links expire after
  7 days and are single use. Resending replaces the link.
- **Statuses** are `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked`, and `expired`. Acceptance and revocation are final. Expiry is based
  on time, and an expired invitation can still be resent or revoked. Accepted and revoked invitations cannot be changed.
- **One live invitation per address.** An address cannot be invited while it has a pending invitation or already
  belongs to a user of the business. Expired and revoked invitations do not count.
- **Customer registration is refused** for an address with a pending invitation (`422 validation_failed`).
- **Accepting** does not require a password reset or another email. Accepting creates a verified user with the invited
  role, and the user signs in with `POST /sessions` as usual.
- **Previews** return `{invitation_preview: {email, role, business_name, subdomain, expires_at}}`. An unknown, expired,
  used, or revoked token returns `422 invalid_token`, and all of those look the same.
- **Suspending** a user signs them out of every session, clears their ticket assignments, and blocks sign-in with
  `403 user_suspended`. Restoring them with `{"user":{"suspended":false}}` allows sign-in again. Suspension does not change
  anyone's requests.
- **The last active admin** cannot be suspended (`422 validation_failed`). Suspended admins do not count as active.
- Only `suspended` can be changed through `PATCH /users/:id`. Roles are fixed when the user is created.

## Account lifecycle

- Only the owner (the admin who registered the business) can cancel or reactivate.
- Cancelling revokes every session in the business. Ordinary access stops: the portal, sign-in for
  other users, and everything except the endpoints above return `403 account_cancelled`.
- The owner can still sign in while cancelled, but only until 90 days have passed, and only to reactivate.
- Accounts still cancelled after 90 days are deleted with all their users and sessions. Run this daily:

      bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts

## Security notes

- Only SHA-256 digests of session, verification, and reset tokens are stored.
- Verification links expire after 3 days and reset links after 2 hours. Both are single use.
- Passwords need at least 8 characters.
- Only SHA-256 digests of invitation tokens are stored. Invitation links expire after 7 days and are single use.

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[admin api app assets mail static status support www].freeze

  # Raised when registration input is invalid. `details` maps field names
  # (owner fields are prefixed, e.g. "admin.email") to their messages.
  class RegistrationInvalid < StandardError
    attr_reader :details

    def initialize(details)
      @details = details
      sentences = details.flat_map do |field, messages|
        messages.map { |message| "#{field.to_s.tr(".", " ").humanize} #{message}" }
      end
      super(sentences.to_sentence)
    end
  end

  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: {maximum: 120}
  validates :subdomain, presence: true,
    format: {with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens"},
    exclusion: {in: RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS, message: "is reserved"},
    uniqueness: true

  scope :cancelled, -> { where.not(cancelled_at: nil) }

  # Creates a business and its owner (an admin) in one transaction. The owner's
  # email is not verified yet. Callers send the verification email afterwards.
  def self.register!(name:, subdomain:, admin:)
    account = new(name:, subdomain:)
    owner = User.new(account:, role: "admin", name: admin[:name], email: admin[:email],
      password: admin[:password].to_s)

    account_valid = account.valid?
    owner_valid = owner.valid?
    unless account_valid && owner_valid
      details = account.errors.to_hash
      owner.errors.to_hash.each { |field, messages| details[:"admin.#{field}"] = messages }
      raise RegistrationInvalid, details
    end

    transaction do
      account.save!
      owner.save!
      account.update!(owner:)
    end
    account
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    raise RegistrationInvalid.new(subdomain: ["has already been taken"])
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts that have been cancelled for longer than the
  # reactivation window, including their users and sessions. Returns how many were deleted.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - REACTIVATION_WINDOW
    purged = 0

    where(cancelled_at: ..cutoff).find_each do |account|
      account.with_lock do
        # Re-check under the row lock in case the owner reactivated in the meantime.
        next unless account.cancelled_at && account.cancelled_at <= cutoff

        account.destroy!
        purged += 1
      end
    end

    Rails.logger.info("[helpdesk] purged #{purged} cancelled account(s)") if purged.positive?
    purged
  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def status
    cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active"
  end

  # When a cancelled account is permanently deleted. Nil while active.
  def reactivate_until
    cancelled_at + REACTIVATION_WINDOW if cancelled?
  end

  def reactivation_open?(now: Time.current)
    cancelled? && now < reactivate_until
  end

  # Cancelling revokes every session in the business. Only the owner can sign in afterwards,
  # and only to reactivate.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      UserSession.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end
end

# single-use token. Only its digest is stored, so a leaked database does not reveal usable links.
#
# Status is derived from the timestamps: accepted, then revoked, then expired (past expires_at),
# and otherwise pending. At most one pending invitation exists for an address in a business.

  TTL = 7.days
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  class LastAdmin < StandardError; end

  scope :staff, -> { where(role: STAFF_ROLES) }
  scope :admins, -> { where(role: "admin") }

  # Customers sign themselves up through a business's portal. The role is always "customer",
  # and the address is unverified until the emailed link is confirmed. An address with a pending
  # invitation belongs to that invitation, so it cannot be registered here.
  def self.register_customer!(account, name:, email:, password:)
    user = account.users.new(name:, email:, password:, role: "customer")
    account.with_lock do
      if account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: user.email)
        user.errors.add(:email, "is reserved for a pending invitation")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user
      end
      user.save!
    end
    user
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # A concurrent registration with the same email won the unique index.
    user.errors.add(:email, "has already been taken")
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user
  end

  # Token lookups match only unexpired tokens, and only within the given business.
  def self.with_email_verification_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.users.find_by(
      email_verification_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      email_verification_sent_at: (now - EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL)..
    )
  end

  def self.with_password_reset_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.users.find_by(
      password_reset_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      password_reset_sent_at: (now - PASSWORD_RESET_TTL)..
    )
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  # Admins and agents work the business's tickets. Customers only see their own requests.
  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  # Suspends or restores this user. Suspending signs the user out everywhere and clears their ticket
  # assignments. Neither changes a customer's request: the assignments are internal, and the tickets'
  # updated_at is left as it was. A business must keep one active admin, so the last one cannot be
  # suspended. The business row is locked so that two concurrent suspensions cannot both pass that check.
  def set_suspended!(value)
    transaction do
      account.lock!
      reload

      raise LastAdmin if value && admin? && account.users.admins.active.where.not(id:).none?

      update!(suspended: value)
      if value
        UserSession.where(user_id: id).delete_all
        Ticket.where(assignee_id: id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
      end
    end
  end

  # Issues a new verification link, replacing any earlier one, and emails it.
  def send_email_verification!
    token = issue_email_verification_token!

      save!(context: :new_password)

class UserSession < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user

  # Set only on the instance returned by start!. The database stores just the digest.
  attr_accessor :token

  def self.start!(user)
    token = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    session = new(user:, token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(token))
    session.token = token
    session.save!
    session
  end

  # Only sessions belonging to users of `account` are found, so a token from one business
  # cannot be used in another.
  def self.find_for_account(account, raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    joins(:user).where(users: {account_id: account.id})
      .find_by(token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw))
  end
end

  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  # Passed as `assignee_id:` or `priority:` to staff_update! to leave that field as it is.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}
  validates :priority, inclusion: {in: PRIORITIES}

  # Most recently active first. Public replies and status changes touch updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched.
  # The text is literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. The EXISTS subquery means a
  # ticket appears once however many comments match.
  def self.search(text)
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern:)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public = TRUE AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  end

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open")
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), optional status change, and
  # optional assignment (an active staff member's ID, or nil to unassign) and priority. A reply alone
  # never changes the status. Assignment and priority are internal, so they do not touch updated_at.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, changes: {}, assignee_id: UNCHANGED, priority: UNCHANGED)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true)) if comment.present?
      update!(changes) if changes.any?
      assign_internally!(assignee_id) unless assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
      prioritize_internally!(priority) unless priority.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end
  end

  private

  # Sets the assignee with update_columns, which skips updated_at. The assignee must be an active
  # staff member of this business.
  def assign_internally!(assignee_id)
    assignee = nil
    unless assignee_id.nil?
      assignee = account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: assignee_id) if valid_id?(assignee_id)
      unless assignee
        errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
      end
    end

    update_columns(assignee_id: assignee&.id)
    association(:assignee).reset
  end

  # Sets the priority with update_columns, which skips updated_at, as assignment does. update_columns
  # skips validations, so the value is checked here.
  def prioritize_internally!(value)
    unless PRIORITIES.include?(value)
      errors.add(:priority, "must be normal or high")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
    end

    update_columns(priority: value)
  end

  def valid_id?(value)
    value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A\d{1,18}\z/)
  end
end

  "output": "# An invitation for a person to join a business as an admin or agent. The emailed link carries a
# single-use token. Only its digest is stored, so a leaked database does not reveal usable links.
#
# Status is derived from the timestamps: accepted, then revoked, then expired (past expires_at),
# and otherwise pending. At most one pending invitation exists for an address in a business.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze
  # The same answer for an unknown, expired, used or revoked link, so links cannot be probed.
  INVALID_LINK_MESSAGE = "This invitation link is invalid or has expired.".freeze

  # Raised when an invitation is already accepted or revoked, so it can no longer be resent or revoked.
  class Closed < StandardError
    attr_reader :status

    def initialize(status)
      @status = status
      super("This invitation was already #{status}.")
    end
  end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true
  belongs_to :accepted_user, class_name: "User", optional: true

  # The raw token exists only on the instance that issued it, for the email. It is never stored.
  attr_accessor :token

  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: {maximum: 254}, format: {with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP}
  validates :role, inclusion: {in: User::STAFF_ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent"}
  validate :email_available, on: %i[create reissue]

  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) {
    where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where(arel_table[:expires_at].gt(now))
  }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) {
    where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where(arel_table[:expires_at].lteq(now))
  }

  def self.with_status(status, now: Time.current)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending(now)
    when "expired" then expired(now)
    when "accepted" then where.not(accepted_at: nil)
    when "revoked" then where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status #{status.inspect}"
    end
  end

  # The pending invitation that a raw token belongs to, within one business.
  def self.pending_for_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.invitations.pending(now).find_by(token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw))
  end

  # Creates an invitation and emails its link. The business row is locked while checking the address,
  # so two admins cannot both invite it (and neither can a customer registration, which takes the same lock).
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
    invitation = nil
    account.with_lock do
      invitation = account.invitations.new(invited_by:, email:, role:)
      invitation.issue_token!(now:)
      invitation.save!
    end
    invitation.send_link!
    invitation
  end

  def status(now: Time.current)
    if accepted_at
      "accepted"
    elsif revoked_at
      "revoked"
    elsif expires_at <= now
      "expired"
    else
      "pending"
    end
  end

  def pending?(now: Time.current)
    status(now:) == "pending"
  end

  # Issues a new link and restarts the expiry. The earlier link stops working.
  def reissue!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!(now:)
      issue_token!(now:)
      save!(context: :reissue)
    end
    send_link!
    self
  end

  # Stops the invitation from being accepted. Pending and expired invitations can be revoked.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      ensure_open!(now:)
      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
    self
  end

  # Creates the user with the invited role and marks the invitation accepted, in one transaction.
  # The emailed link proves control of the address, so the user is verified from the start and
  # does not need another verification email.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise Closed, status(now:) unless pending?(now:)

      user = account.users.new(name:, email:, password:, role:, verified: true)
      user.save!
      update!(accepted_at: now, accepted_user: user)
      user
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # The address became a user of this business after the invitation was checked.
    errors.add(:email, "has already been taken")
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
  end

  def issue_token!(now: Time.current)
    self.token = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    self.token_digest = Helpdesk::Token.digest(token)
    self.sent_at = now
    self.expires_at = now + TTL
  end

  def send_link!
    InvitationMailer.invitation(self, token).deliver_now
  end

  private

  # Accepted and revoked invitations are final. Pending and expired ones can still be resent or revoked.
  def ensure_open!(now:)
    current = status(now:)
    raise Closed, current if %w[accepted revoked].include?(current)
  end

  # Only one live invitation per address, and no invitation for an address that already has a user.
  # Expired invitations do not count.
  def email_available
    if account.users.exists?(email:)
      errors.add(:email, "already belongs to a user in this business")
    elsif account.invitations.pending.where(email:).where.not(id:).exists?
      errors.add(:email, "already has a pending invitation")
    end
  end
end

      end

        render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only admins can do that.")

      def checked_enum(name, allowed)
        value = params[name]

      # Reads a person's ID from a query string, such as ?requester_id=12. Returns it as an Integer.

      @expected = expected
      super("#{field} must be #{expected}.")

  rescue_from InvalidShape do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: {error.field => ["must be #{error.expected}"]})
  end

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    render_error(404, "not_found", "The requested record was not found.")
  end

  def render_error(status, code, message, details: nil)
    error = {code:, message:}
    error[:details] = details if details.present?
    render json: {error:}, status:
  end

  # Reads a required envelope such as {"user": {...}}, keeping only the listed fields.
  # Nested hashes are described as keyword arguments, e.g. envelope(:account, :name, admin: [:email]).
  # A listed field of the wrong shape is refused. permit would otherwise drop it without a word.
  def envelope(key, *fields, **nested)
    value = params.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key) unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    fields.each do |field|
      next unless value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || value[field].is_a?(Array)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "a single value")
    end
    nested.each_key do |field|
      next if value[field].nil? || value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "an object")
    end

    value.permit(*fields, **nested)
  end

        tickets = tickets.where(status: checked_enum(:status, Ticket::STATUSES)) if params[:status].present?

module Helpdesk
  # Allows browsers served from the configured frontend origin to call the API.
  # Requests from any other origin are still processed, but get no CORS headers,
  # so browsers refuse to expose their responses to that page.
  class Cors
    ALLOWED_METHODS = "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS".freeze
    ALLOWED_HEADERS = "Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, X-Helpdesk-Account".freeze
    MAX_AGE = "600".freeze

    def initialize(app)
      @app = app
    end

    def call(env)
      origin = env["HTTP_ORIGIN"]
      return @app.call(env) if origin.nil?

      allowed = origin == Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_origin

      if preflight?(env)
        return [allowed ? 204 : 403, cors_headers(origin, allowed), []]
      end

      status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
      [status, headers.merge(cors_headers(origin, allowed)), body]
    end

    private

    def preflight?(env)
      env["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "OPTIONS" && env["HTTP_ACCESS_CONTROL_REQUEST_METHOD"].present?
    end

    def cors_headers(origin, allowed)
      headers = {"vary" => "Origin"}
      return headers unless allowed

      headers.merge(
        "access-control-allow-origin" => origin,
        "access-control-allow-methods" => ALLOWED_METHODS,
        "access-control-allow-headers" => ALLOWED_HEADERS,
        "access-control-max-age" => MAX_AGE
      )
    end
  end
end

  # Runtime configuration. Values are read from the environment on each call so

  module Settings
    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze
    DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test".freeze

require_relative "../config/environment"
require "rails/test_help"

module HelpdeskTestHelpers
  HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account"
  PASSWORD = "my-first-password"
  NEW_PASSWORD = "my-new-password"

  # Performs a request against the JSON API. Pass `account:` for the business
  # header and `token:` for the bearer session token.
  def api(method, path, body: nil, account: nil, token: nil)
    headers = {"Accept" => "application/json"}
    headers[HEADER] = account if account
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token

    if body
      send(method, path, params: body, headers: headers, as: :json)
    else
      send(method, path, headers: headers)
    end
  end

  def json
    response.parsed_body
  end

  def signup(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, admin_name: "Jo")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/account/create", body: {
      account: {name:, subdomain:, admin: {name: admin_name, email:, password:}}
    })
  end

  # Signs up a business and confirms the owner's email. Returns the owner.
  def verified_owner(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD)
    signup(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    assert_response :created
    token = link_token(last_mail)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm", body: {email_verification: {token:}}, account: subdomain)
    assert_response :ok
    Account.find_by!(subdomain:).users.find_by!(email:)
  end

  def sign_in(email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, account: "acme")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/sessions", body: {session: {email:, password:}}, account:)
    assert_response :created
    json.dig("session", "token")
  end

  CUSTOMER_PASSWORD = "my-customer-password"

  # Registers a customer through the portal and confirms the emailed link. Returns the customer.
  def verified_customer(account: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    register_customer(account:, name:, email:, password:)
    assert_response :created
    token = link_token(last_mail)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm", body: {email_verification: {token:}}, account:)
    assert_response :ok
    Account.find_by!(subdomain: account).users.find_by!(email:)
  end

  def register_customer(account: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/registrations", body: {user: {name:, email:, password:}}, account:)
  end

  # Signs in a verified customer and returns the bearer token.
  def customer_token(account: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    sign_in(email:, password:, account:)
  end

  # Opens a request as the customer behind `token`. Returns the request's ID.
  def open_request(token:, subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.", account: "acme")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/requests", body: {request: {subject:, comment: {body:}}}, account:, token:)
    assert_response :created
    json.dig("request", "id")
  end

  def last_mail
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
  end

  def link_token(mail)
    mail.body.decoded[/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/, 1]
  end

  def header(name)
    response.headers.to_h.transform_keys(&:downcase)[name.downcase]
  end

  # Temporarily sets environment variables for the duration of the block.
  def with_env(vars)
    saved = vars.keys.to_h { |key| [key, ENV[key]] }
    vars.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
    yield
  ensure
    saved.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
  end

  class Base
    include ActiveSupport::Rescuable
    include ActionMailbox::Callbacks, ActionMailbox::Routing

        track_status_of_inbound_email do
          run_callbacks :process do
            process
          end
        end
      rescue => exception
        rescue_with_handler(exception) || raise
      end

    end

      inbound_email.delivered? || inbound_email.bounced?

module ActionMailbox
  module Callbacks
    extend  ActiveSupport::Concern
    include ActiveSupport::Callbacks
    TERMINATOR = ->(mailbox, chain) do
      chain.call
      mailbox.finished_processing?
    end
    included do
      define_callbacks :process, terminator: TERMINATOR, skip_after_callbacks_if_terminated: true
    end
    class_methods do
      def before_processing(*methods, &block)
        set_callback(:process, :before, *methods, &block)
      end
      def after_processing(*methods, &block)
        set_callback(:process, :after, *methods, &block)
      end
      def around_processing(*methods, &block)

    end

require "mail"
module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable
    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]
    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end
    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end
    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end
    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# The +Message-ID+ as specified by rfc822 is supposed to be a unique identifier for that individual email.
# That makes it an ideal tracking token for debugging and forensics, just like +X-Request-Id+ does for
# web request.
#
# If an inbound email does not, against the rfc822 mandate, specify a Message-ID, one will be generated
# using the approach from +Mail::MessageIdField+.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::MessageId
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  class_methods do
    # Create a new +InboundEmail+ from the raw +source+ of the email, which is uploaded as an Active Storage
    # attachment called +raw_email+. Before the upload, extract the Message-ID from the +source+ and set
    # it as an attribute on the new +InboundEmail+.
    def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
      message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(source)
      message_id = extract_message_id(source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)
      create! raw_email: create_and_upload_raw_email!(source),
        message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum, **options
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      nil
    end
    private
      def extract_message_id(source)
        Mail.from_source(source).message_id rescue nil
      end
      def generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)
        Mail::MessageIdField.new("<#{message_checksum}@#{::Socket.gethostname}.mail>").message_id.tap do |message_id|
          logger.warn "Message-ID couldn't be parsed or is missing. Generated a new Message-ID: #{message_id}"
        end
      end
      def create_and_upload_raw_email!(source)
        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload! io: StringIO.new(source), filename: "message.eml", content_type: "message/rfc822",
                                               service_name: ActionMailbox.storage_service
      end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# A newly received +InboundEmail+ will not be routed synchronously as part of ingress controller's receival.
# Instead, the routing will be done asynchronously, using a +RoutingJob+, to ensure maximum parallel capacity.
#
# By default, all newly created +InboundEmail+ records that have the status of +pending+, which is the default,
# will be scheduled for automatic, deferred routing.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::Routable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  included do
    after_create_commit :route_later, if: :pending?
  end
  # Enqueue a +RoutingJob+ for this +InboundEmail+.
  def route_later
    ActionMailbox::RoutingJob.perform_later self
  end
  # Route this +InboundEmail+ using the routing rules declared on the +ApplicationMailbox+.
  def route
    ApplicationMailbox.route self
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# Ensure that the +InboundEmail+ is automatically scheduled for later incineration if the status has been
# changed to +processed+. The later incineration will be invoked at the time specified by the
# +ActionMailbox.incinerate_after+ time using the +IncinerationJob+.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::Incineratable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  included do
    after_update_commit :incinerate_later, if: -> { ActionMailbox.incinerate && status_previously_changed? && processed? }
  end
  def incinerate_later
    ActionMailbox::IncinerationJob.schedule self
  end
  def incinerate
    Incineration.new(self).run
  end

module ActionMailbox
  # Ingests inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server.
  #
  # Authenticates requests using HTTP basic access authentication. The username is always +actionmailbox+, and the
  # password is read from the application's encrypted credentials or an environment variable. See the Usage section below.
  #
  # Note that basic authentication is insecure over unencrypted HTTP. An attacker that intercepts cleartext requests to
  # the ingress can learn its password. You should only use this ingress over HTTPS.
  #
  # Returns:
  #
  # - <tt>204 No Content</tt> if an inbound email is successfully recorded and enqueued for routing to the appropriate mailbox
  # - <tt>401 Unauthorized</tt> if the request could not be authenticated
  # - <tt>404 Not Found</tt> if Action Mailbox is not configured to accept inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server
  # - <tt>415 Unsupported Media Type</tt> if the request does not contain an RFC 822 message
  # - <tt>500 Server Error</tt> if the ingress password is not configured, or if one of the Active Record database,
  #   the Active Storage service, or the Active Job backend is misconfigured or unavailable
  #
  # == Usage
  #
  # 1. Tell Action Mailbox to accept emails from an SMTP relay:
  #
  #        # config/environments/production.rb
  #        config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay
  #
  # 2. Generate a strong password that Action Mailbox can use to authenticate requests to the ingress.
  #
  #    Use <tt>bin/rails credentials:edit</tt> to add the password to your application's encrypted credentials under
  #    +action_mailbox.ingress_password+, where Action Mailbox will automatically find it:
  #
  #        action_mailbox:
  #          ingress_password: ...
  #
  #    Alternatively, provide the password in the +RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD+ environment variable.
  #
  # 3. Configure your SMTP server to pipe inbound emails to the appropriate ingress command, providing the +URL+ of the
  #    relay ingress and the +INGRESS_PASSWORD+ you previously generated.
  #
  #    If your application lives at <tt>https://example.com</tt>, you would configure the Postfix SMTP server to pipe
  #    inbound emails to the following command:
  #
  #        $ bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix URL=https://example.com/rails/action_mailbox/postfix/inbound_emails INGRESS_PASSWORD=...
  #
  #    Built-in ingress commands are available for these popular SMTP servers:
  #
  #    - Exim (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:exim</tt>)
  #    - Postfix (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix</tt>)
  #    - Qmail (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:qmail</tt>)
  class Ingresses::Relay::InboundEmailsController < ActionMailbox::BaseController
    before_action :authenticate_by_password, :require_valid_rfc822_message

    def create
      if request.body
        ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.create_and_extract_message_id! request.body.read
      else
        head ActionDispatch::Constants::UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT
      end
    end

    private
      def require_valid_rfc822_message
        unless request.media_type == "message/rfc822"
          head :unsupported_media_type
        end
      end
  end
end

module ActionMailbox
  # Routing a new InboundEmail is an asynchronous operation, which allows the ingress controllers to quickly
  # accept new incoming emails without being burdened to hang while they're actually being processed.
  class RoutingJob < ActiveJob::Base

module ActionMailbox
  # = Action Mailbox \Router
  #
  # Encapsulates the routes that live on the ApplicationMailbox and performs the actual routing when
  # an inbound_email is received.
  class Router
    class RoutingError < StandardError; end
    def initialize
      @routes = []
    end
    def add_routes(routes)
      routes.each do |(address, mailbox_name)|
        add_route address, to: mailbox_name
      end
    end
    def add_route(address, to:)
      routes.append Route.new(address, to: to)
    end
    def route(inbound_email)
      if mailbox = mailbox_for(inbound_email)
        mailbox.receive(inbound_email)
      else
        inbound_email.bounced!
        raise RoutingError
      end
    end
    def mailbox_for(inbound_email)
      routes.detect { |route| route.match?(inbound_email) }&.mailbox_class
    end
    private
      attr_reader :routes
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
module ActionMailbox
  # Encapsulates a route, which can then be matched against an inbound_email and provide a lookup of the matching
  # mailbox class. See examples for the different route addresses and how to use them in the ActionMailbox::Base
  # documentation.
  class Router::Route
    attr_reader :address, :mailbox_name
    def initialize(address, to:)
      @address, @mailbox_name = address, to
      ensure_valid_address
    end
    def match?(inbound_email)
      case address
      when :all
        true
      when String
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.casecmp?(recipient) }
      when Regexp
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.match?(recipient) }
      when Proc
        address.call(inbound_email)
      else
        address.match?(inbound_email)
      end
    end
    def mailbox_class
      "#{mailbox_name.to_s.camelize}Mailbox".constantize
    end
    private
      def ensure_valid_address
        unless [ Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc ].any? { |klass| address.is_a?(klass) } || address.respond_to?(:match?)
          raise ArgumentError, "Expected a Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc, or matchable, got #{address.inspect}"
        end
      end
  end
end

module Mail
  class Message
    def from_address
      address_list(header[:from])&.addresses&.first
    end
    def reply_to_address
      address_list(header[:reply_to])&.addresses&.first
    end
    def recipients_addresses
      to_addresses + cc_addresses + bcc_addresses + x_original_to_addresses + x_forwarded_to_addresses

    def to_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:to])&.addresses)

      Array(address_list(header[:cc])&.addresses)
    end
    def bcc_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:bcc])&.addresses)
    end
    def x_original_to_addresses
      Array(header[:x_original_to]).collect { |header| Mail::Address.new header.to_s }

      Array(header[:x_forwarded_to]).collect { |header| Mail::Address.new header.to_s }

        if obj.respond_to?(:element)

          obj.element

# frozen_string_literal: true
module ActionMailbox
  # You can configure when this +IncinerationJob+ will be run as a time-after-processing using the
  # +config.action_mailbox.incinerate_after+ or +ActionMailbox.incinerate_after+ setting.
  #
  # Since this incineration is set for the future, it'll automatically ignore any <tt>InboundEmail</tt>s
  # that have already been deleted and discard itself if so.
  #
  # You can disable incinerating processed emails by setting +config.action_mailbox.incinerate+ or
  # +ActionMailbox.incinerate+ to +false+.
  class IncinerationJob < ActiveJob::Base
    queue_as { ActionMailbox.queues[:incineration] }
    discard_on ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    def self.schedule(inbound_email)
      set(wait: ActionMailbox.incinerate_after).perform_later(inbound_email)
    end
    def perform(inbound_email)
      inbound_email.incinerate
    end
  end
end

  # Command class for carrying out the actual incineration of the +InboundMail+ that's been scheduled

# 1. application.rb: load Active Storage + Action Mailbox and enable the relay ingress.

s = s.replace('# require "active_storage/engine"', 'require "active_storage/engine"', 1)
s = s.replace('# require "action_mailbox/engine"', 'require "action_mailbox/engine"', 1)
s = s.replace(
    '    config.api_only = true\n',
    '    config.api_only = true\n\n'

    '    # authenticated with RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD.\n'
    '    config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay\n', 1)
p.write_text(s)

# 2. Active Storage service: raw emails are stored there. Development and production use disk storage/.
for name in ["development", "production"]:
    p = pathlib.Path(f"config/environments/{name}.rb")
    s = p.read_text()
    marker = "  config.action_mailer.delivery_method"
    assert marker in s, name
    s = s.replace(marker,
        "  # Raw inbound emails (Action Mailbox) are kept on local disk under storage/.\n"
        "  config.active_storage.service = :local\n\n" + marker, 1)
    p.write_text(s)

Next I'll write the pure helpers for inbound mail: recipient parsing, sender checks, automated-mail detection, and body/subject extraction. These don't touch the database.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > lib/helpdesk/inbound_mail.rb <<'EOF'
require "loofah"

module Helpdesk
  # Reads an inbound email for the support mailbox: who it is addressed to, who sent it, and the subject
  # and plain-text message to store. Nothing here touches the database.
  module InboundMail
    # A recipient on the support domain. `tag` is the part after "+" in the local part (a reply address), or nil.
    Recipient = Data.define(:subdomain, :tag)

    LOCAL_PART = /\A(?<subdomain>[^+@\s]+)(?:\+(?<tag>[^+@\s]+))?\z/
    AUTOMATED_SENDER = /\A(mailer-daemon|postmaster|bounces?|(no|do-?not)-?reply)\z/
    AUTOMATED_HEADERS = %w[x-auto-response-suppress x-autoreply x-autorespond].freeze
    BULK_PRECEDENCE = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply].freeze

    module_function

    # Every recipient on the support domain: To, Cc, Bcc and the forwarding headers the mail gem reads.
    def support_recipients(mail)
      domain = Helpdesk::Settings.support_domain
      mail.recipients_addresses.filter_map do |address|
        next unless address.domain.to_s.downcase == domain

        match = LOCAL_PART.match(address.local.to_s.downcase)
        Recipient.new(subdomain: match[:subdomain], tag: match[:tag]) if match
      end
    end

    # Lowercase addresses from the From header.
    def from_addresses(mail)
      Array(mail.from).map { |address| address.to_s.strip.downcase }.reject(&:blank?)
    end

    # The sender's address when it is a usable one, else nil.
    def sender_address(mail)
      address = from_addresses(mail).first
      address if valid_address?(address)
    end

    def valid_address?(address)
      address.present? && address.length <= 254 && URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP.match?(address)
    end

    # The From display name, or the address's local part when the sender gave no name.
    def sender_name(mail, address)
      name = clean_line(mail.from_address&.display_name)
      name = address.split("@").first if name.blank?
      name.truncate(User::NAME_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "")
    end

    def subject(mail)
      clean_line(mail.subject).truncate(Ticket::SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "").presence || "(no subject)"
    end

    # The plain-text message. Uses the text/plain part, or the HTML part converted to text.
    def text_body(mail)
      text = utf8(plain_text(mail)).delete("\u0000").gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
      text.truncate(Comment::BODY_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "").presence || "(no message text)"
    end

    # Automated and list mail (auto-replies, bounces, notifications, newsletters). It is not a support request.
    def automated?(mail)
      names = mail.header.fields.map { |field| field.name.downcase }
      return true if names.any? { |name| name.start_with?("list-") } || names.intersect?(AUTOMATED_HEADERS)

      auto_submitted = mail.header["Auto-Submitted"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase
      return true if auto_submitted.present? && auto_submitted != "no"
      return true if BULK_PRECEDENCE.include?(mail.header["Precedence"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase)
      return true if mail.mime_type == "multipart/report"
      # An empty Return-Path (<>) is the null sender that bounces and auto-replies use.
      return true if mail.header["Return-Path"] && mail.header["Return-Path"].value.to_s.strip.empty?

      local = from_addresses(mail).first.to_s.split("@").first.to_s.split("+").first.to_s
      AUTOMATED_SENDER.match?(local)
    end

    def plain_text(mail)
      parts = mail.multipart? ? mail.all_parts.reject(&:multipart?) : [mail]

      plain = parts.find { |part| !part.attachment? && (part.mime_type.nil? || part.mime_type == "text/plain") }
      return decode(plain) if plain

      html = parts.find { |part| !part.attachment? && part.mime_type == "text/html" }
      html ? html_to_text(decode(html)) : ""
    end

    def decode(part)
      part.decoded.to_s
    rescue StandardError
      part.body.raw_source.to_s
    end

    # Turns line breaks and paragraph ends into newlines, drops script, style and head content, and
    # decodes entities.
    def html_to_text(html)
      html = html.gsub(%r{<br\s*/?>}i, "\n").gsub(%r{</(p|div|li|tr|h[1-6])\s*>}i, "\n")
      fragment = Loofah.fragment(html)
      fragment.xpath(".//script|.//style|.//head|.//title").each(&:remove)
      fragment.text(encode_special_chars: false)
    end

    def clean_line(text)
      utf8(text).delete("\u0000").gsub(/[[:space:]]+/, " ").strip
    end

    # Converts text to valid UTF-8, replacing bytes that cannot be read, so it can be stored.
    def utf8(text)
      text = text.to_s
      case text.encoding
      when Encoding::UTF_8 then text.scrub("?")
      when Encoding::BINARY then text.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub("?")
      else text.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "?")
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: Now the `Ticket` model. It gets a source (`portal` or `email`), a per-ticket reply token, a `reply_address`, and a hook so that public staff replies on email tickets are mailed to the requester. Private notes and status-only changes are not. I'll rewrite the file in full, keeping the existing methods unchanged.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/ticket.rb <<'EOF'
class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # "portal" for requests opened in the portal. "email" for tickets opened from inbound mail, whose public
  # replies are emailed to the requester.
  SOURCES = %w[portal email].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  # Passed as `assignee_id:` or `priority:` to staff_update! to leave that field as it is.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}
  validates :priority, inclusion: {in: PRIORITIES}
  validates :source, inclusion: {in: SOURCES}

  before_validation :assign_reply_token, on: :create

  # Most recently active first. Public replies and status changes touch updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched.
  # The text is literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. The EXISTS subquery means a
  # ticket appears once however many comments match.
  def self.search(text)
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern:)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public = TRUE AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  end

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:, source: "portal")
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open", source:)
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  def email?
    source == "email"
  end

  # The private address for this conversation, e.g. acme+<token>@support.example.test. Mail sent here is a reply
  # from the requester, and it lands on this ticket.
  def reply_address
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_address(account.subdomain, tag: reply_token)
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), optional status change, and
  # optional assignment (an active staff member's ID, or nil to unassign) and priority. A reply alone
  # never changes the status. Assignment and priority are internal, so they do not touch updated_at.
  # A public reply on an email ticket is also emailed to the requester, after the update is saved.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, changes: {}, assignee_id: UNCHANGED, priority: UNCHANGED)
    reply = nil
    transaction do
      reply = comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true)) if comment.present?
      update!(changes) if changes.any?
      assign_internally!(assignee_id) unless assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
      prioritize_internally!(priority) unless priority.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end
    email_reply_to_requester(reply) if reply&.public?
  end

  private

  def assign_reply_token
    self.reply_token ||= SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  # Suspended requesters are cut off from the email channel, so their replies are not sent.
  def email_reply_to_requester(reply)
    return unless email? && !requester.suspended?

    TicketMailer.reply(reply).deliver_later
  end

  # Sets the assignee with update_columns, which skips updated_at. The assignee must be an active
  # staff member of this business.
  def assign_internally!(assignee_id)
    assignee = nil
    unless assignee_id.nil?
      assignee = account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: assignee_id) if valid_id?(assignee_id)
      unless assignee
        errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
      end
    end

    update_columns(assignee_id: assignee&.id)
    association(:assignee).reset
  end

  # Sets the priority with update_columns, which skips updated_at, as assignment does. update_columns
  # skips validations, so the value is checked here.
  def prioritize_internally!(value)
    unless PRIORITIES.include?(value)
      errors.add(:priority, "must be normal or high")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
    end

    update_columns(priority: value)
  end

  def valid_id?(value)
    value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A\d{1,18}\z/)
  end
end
EOF

class TicketMailer < ApplicationMailer
  # A public staff reply on an email ticket, sent to the requester. Reply-To is the ticket's private address,
  # so the requester's next email comes back to this conversation.
  def reply(comment)
    @comment = comment
    @ticket = comment.ticket
    @requester = @ticket.requester
    @account = @ticket.account

    subject = @ticket.subject
    subject = "Re: #{subject}" unless subject.match?(/\Are:/i)
    mail(to: @requester.email, subject:, reply_to: @ticket.reply_address)
  end
end

steps.message: Now the core piece, `SupportMailbox`. It applies the rules in order: skip automated mail, resolve a single business from all support-domain recipients, then either route a reply to its ticket (only if the sender is the requester) or open a new ticket. Every rejection rolls back its work and is recorded as `bounced`, which doesn't block a later valid retry.

# Turns mail sent to a business's support address into a ticket, and mail sent to a ticket's private reply
# address into a reply from the requester.
#
# A delivery that cannot be used is rejected. Its changes roll back, and the inbound email is recorded as
# bounced. A bounced delivery does not block a later delivery with the same Message-ID, so a retry that becomes
# valid (for example, after the business signs up) is processed. Only deliveries that produced a ticket or a
# reply count as delivered, and only those block duplicates.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  # Raised to reject a delivery. Changes made inside a transaction roll back with it.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  def process
    reject!("automated or list mail") if Helpdesk::InboundMail.automated?(mail)

    account = business
    ticket = conversation(account)
    ticket ? reply_from_requester(ticket) : open_ticket(account)
  rescue Rejected => error
    logger.info("[helpdesk] inbound email #{inbound_email.id} rejected: #{error.message}")
    inbound_email.bounced!
  end

  private

  # The one business this mail is for, found from every support-domain recipient (To, Cc and Bcc).
  # Mail addressed to several businesses is ignored, and so is mail addressed to none.
  def business
    subdomains = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).map(&:subdomain).uniq
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    reject!("no business at the recipient addresses") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to #{accounts.size} businesses") if accounts.size > 1

    account = accounts.first
    reject!("business #{account.subdomain} is cancelled") if account.cancelled?
    account
  end

  # The ticket whose private reply address this mail was sent to, or nil. Mail to two different conversations
  # is ambiguous and is rejected.
  def conversation(account)
    tags = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).filter_map do |recipient|
      recipient.tag if recipient.subdomain == account.subdomain
    end
    tickets = account.tickets.where(reply_token: tags).includes(:requester).to_a
    reject!("reply addresses point at several tickets") if tickets.size > 1

    tickets.first
  end

  # Only the requester may reply by email. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a pending or solved ticket.
  def reply_from_requester(ticket)
    requester = ticket.requester
    reject!("sender is not the requester of ticket #{ticket.id}") unless
      Helpdesk::InboundMail.from_addresses(mail).include?(requester.email)
    reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    ticket.requester_update!(author: requester, comment: {body: text_body})
  end

  # Mail to the plain support address opens a new ticket. A sender who is not yet a user becomes an unverified
  # customer, and is sent a verification email. Email never verifies anyone.
  def open_ticket(account)
    sender = Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_address(mail)
    reject!("no valid sender address") unless sender

    account.with_lock do
      requester, created = register_requester(account, sender)
      reject!("sender is #{requester.role}, not a customer") unless requester.customer?
      reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

      Ticket.open!(requester:, subject: Helpdesk::InboundMail.subject(mail), body: text_body, source: "email")
      # Sent inside the transaction: if the email cannot be sent, nothing is saved and a retry starts clean.
      requester.send_email_verification! if created
    end
  end

  def register_requester(account, sender)
    User.customer_for_email!(account, name: Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_name(mail, sender), email: sender)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    reject!("sender could not be registered: #{error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence}")
  end

  def text_body
    @text_body ||= Helpdesk::InboundMail.text_body(mail)
  end

  def reject!(reason)
    raise Rejected, reason
  end
end
EOF

steps.message:
All 37 integration tests pass. Before finishing, I want to re-examine one design choice, because it has a real failure mode.

The current dedupe relies on `InboundEmail` rows holding a Message-ID. If the process dies while routing, that row stays `pending` and the unique index blocks every relay retry. The retry then gets a silent 204 and the mail is lost. The spec's "invalid deliveries must not block a retry" points the same way.

A more robust approach is to record the Message-ID on the comment that the delivery creates, in the same transaction. Then:
- A rejected or crashed delivery creates no comment, so it can never block a retry.
- A duplicate is caught by a unique index on that comment, so it cannot create a second ticket.
- The dedupe record persists after the raw email is incinerated.

I'll switch to that. The `InboundEmail` index becomes a plain, non-unique index, since the old composite unique index would also let a bounced delivery block a retry. I'll roll back my two unshipped migrations, edit them, and add a comments migration.

# Action Mailbox's stock index is unique on [message_id, message_checksum]. Two problems with it:
#
# * A redelivery usually gains a Received header, so its checksum differs and the message would not be
#   recognised as a duplicate.
# * A row for a rejected or failed delivery would block a later valid retry of the same bytes.
#
# So the index is not unique. Duplicates are recognised by the Message-ID recorded on the comment that a
# delivery creates (see AddInboundMessageIdToComments), which only happens for a delivery that succeeds.
class RelaxInboundEmailUniqueness < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def up
    remove_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, name: "index_action_mailbox_inbound_emails_uniqueness"
    add_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, :message_id
  end

  def down
    remove_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, :message_id
    add_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, [:message_id, :message_checksum], unique: true,
      name: "index_action_mailbox_inbound_emails_uniqueness"
  end
end
EOF
cat > db/migrate/20261119050005_add_inbound_message_id_to_comments.rb <<'EOF'
class AddInboundMessageIdToComments < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def change
    # The Message-ID of the email that created this comment. Only one comment can carry a given Message-ID,
    # so a redelivery of a message that was delivered creates nothing, even after its raw email is incinerated.
    # A delivery that is rejected or fails creates no comment, so it never blocks a later valid retry.
    add_column :comments, :inbound_message_id, :string
    add_index :comments, :inbound_message_id, unique: true, where: "inbound_message_id IS NOT NULL",
      name: "index_comments_on_inbound_message_id"
  end
end

cat > app/mailboxes/support_mailbox.rb <<'EOF'
# Turns mail sent to a business's support address into a ticket, and mail sent to a ticket's private reply
# address into a reply from the requester.
#
# A delivery is recorded as delivered only when it creates a comment. The comment stores the email's Message-ID,
# and only one comment can hold a given Message-ID. So a redelivery of a message that was delivered creates
# nothing, while a rejected, failed or interrupted delivery creates no comment and a later retry is processed.
#
# A rejected delivery's changes roll back and the inbound email is recorded as bounced.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  DUPLICATE_INDEX = "index_comments_on_inbound_message_id".freeze

  # Raised to reject a delivery. Changes made inside a transaction roll back with it.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  def process
    deliver
  rescue Rejected => error
    reject_delivery(error.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique => error
    # A concurrent delivery of the same message saved its comment first. Its comment stands, so this one is a duplicate.
    raise unless error.message.include?(DUPLICATE_INDEX)

    reject_delivery("already delivered")
  end

  private

  def deliver
    reject!("already delivered") if Comment.exists?(inbound_message_id: message_id)
    reject!("automated or list mail") if Helpdesk::InboundMail.automated?(mail)

    account = business
    ticket = conversation(account)
    ticket ? reply_from_requester(ticket) : open_ticket(account)
  end

  def reject_delivery(reason)
    logger.info("[helpdesk] inbound email #{inbound_email.id} rejected: #{reason}")
    inbound_email.bounced!
  end

  def message_id
    inbound_email.message_id
  end

  # The one business this mail is for, found from every support-domain recipient (To, Cc and Bcc).
  # Mail addressed to several businesses is ignored, and so is mail addressed to none.
  def business
    subdomains = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).map(&:subdomain).uniq
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    reject!("no business at the recipient addresses") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to #{accounts.size} businesses") if accounts.size > 1

    account = accounts.first
    reject!("business #{account.subdomain} is cancelled") if account.cancelled?
    account
  end

  # The ticket whose private reply address this mail was sent to, or nil. Mail to two different conversations
  # is ambiguous and is rejected.
  def conversation(account)
    tags = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).filter_map do |recipient|
      recipient.tag if recipient.subdomain == account.subdomain
    end
    tickets = account.tickets.where(reply_token: tags).includes(:requester).to_a
    reject!("reply addresses point at several tickets") if tickets.size > 1

    tickets.first
  end

  # Only the requester may reply by email. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a pending or solved ticket.
  def reply_from_requester(ticket)
    requester = ticket.requester
    from_requester = Helpdesk::InboundMail.from_addresses(mail).include?(requester.email)
    reject!("sender is not the requester of ticket #{ticket.id}") unless from_requester
    reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    ticket.requester_update!(author: requester, comment: {body: text_body}, inbound_message_id: message_id)
  end

  # Mail to the plain support address opens a new ticket. A sender who is not yet a user becomes an unverified
  # customer, and is sent a verification email. Email never verifies anyone.
  def open_ticket(account)
    sender = Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_address(mail)
    reject!("no valid sender address") unless sender

    account.with_lock do
      requester, created = register_requester(account, sender)
      reject!("sender is #{requester.role}, not a customer") unless requester.customer?
      reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

      Ticket.open!(requester:, subject: Helpdesk::InboundMail.subject(mail), body: text_body, source: "email",
        inbound_message_id: message_id)
      # Sent inside the transaction: if the email cannot be sent, nothing is saved and a retry starts clean.
      requester.send_email_verification! if created
    end
  end

  def register_requester(account, sender)
    User.customer_for_email!(account, name: Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_name(mail, sender), email: sender)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    reject!("sender could not be registered: #{error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence}")
  end

  def text_body
    @text_body ||= Helpdesk::InboundMail.text_body(mail)
  end

  def reject!(reason)
    raise Rejected, reason
  end
end
EOF

Re-reading `open_ticket`, I see another robustness problem. The verification email is sent inside the transaction, and `raise_delivery_errors` is on in production. A permanent SMTP rejection (for example, a forged From address that doesn't exist) would roll back the ticket, and every relay retry would fail the same way. The customer's message would be lost. section = '''## Email

Customers can write to support from their mail client. Each business receives mail at `<subdomain>@<HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN>`
(`acme@support.example.test` by default). Every ticket also has a private reply address, `<subdomain>+<token>@<domain>`. A staff
public reply on an email ticket is sent to the requester with `Reply-To` set to that address, so the requester's reply comes back
to the same conversation.

### Inbound relay

Mail arrives through Action Mailbox's relay ingress. The SMTP server posts each raw message to it:

    POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails
    Content-Type: message/rfc822
    Authorization: Basic base64("actionmailbox:$RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD")

It answers `204` once the message is recorded. `401` means the password is wrong, `415` means the content type is not `message/rfc822`.
In test, routing happens inside the request. Elsewhere, routing is an Active Job (`ActionMailbox::RoutingJob`), so production needs a
persistent job backend and a worker running it. The app ships without one, so configure one before taking live mail.

### What happens to a delivery

- **Business.** Every To, Cc and Bcc recipient on the support domain is considered. The mail must address exactly one existing
  business. Mail to several businesses, to none, or to a cancelled business is rejected.
- **Automated and list mail is rejected.** That covers `Auto-Submitted` (other than `no`), `List-*` headers,
  `Precedence: bulk|list|junk|auto_reply`, `X-Auto-Response-Suppress`, `X-Autoreply`, `X-Autorespond`, bounce reports
  (`multipart/report`), an empty `Return-Path`, and senders such as `mailer-daemon@`, `postmaster@` or `no-reply@`.
- **Reply address.** Mail to a ticket's reply address is a reply on that ticket. Only the requester's address may do this. Any
  other sender is rejected. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a `pending` or `solved` ticket. A reply to an unknown reply
  address opens a new ticket.
- **Plain support address.** A new message opens a ticket with the mail's subject, and its plain-text message as the first comment.
  The subject is shortened to 255 characters and the message to 10,000. A missing subject becomes `(no subject)`. A message with
  only HTML is converted to text.
- **Customers.** The sender is matched by address. An existing customer is reused, and receiving mail does not verify anyone.
  A new sender becomes an unverified customer and is sent the verification link. That customer has a random password, so after
  confirming the link they set one with `POST /password_resets`, and then they can sign in. Mail from a staff member, or from a
  suspended customer, is rejected.
- **Deduplication.** The Message-ID of the email is stored on the comment it creates, and only one comment can hold a given
  Message-ID. A redelivery of a message that was delivered creates nothing, and this holds even after the raw email is
  incinerated. A rejected or failed delivery creates no comment, so a later retry of the same message is processed.
- **Requester replies** are not emailed back. Staff replies go out only when the requester is not suspended.

### Maintenance

- Raw emails are kept for 30 days, then deleted (`config.action_mailbox.incinerate_after`). Processed inbound rows are deleted
  with them.
- Duplicate deliveries leave orphan attachments behind. Purge them daily with `bin/rails active_storage:purge_unattached`.
- Raw emails are stored under `storage/` in development and production.

'''
